context.objective: Document how we carry out Investor Onboarding, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: To begin with, we open the onboarding record and assign responsibility. What we do: create the onboarding checklist log, record fund entity, investor legal name, contact, expected commitment, initial subsequent close status, target close date, and client contact. Assign the preparer and investor services team lead reviewer accountable role, identify fund team, treasury, legal, tax, and dependencies. The check on it: one active record exists for the investor fund and ownership is clear.
What event or request prompts you to open the onboarding record?

Next, we establish the required document checklist, what we do, list required subscription, side letter, tax, AML KYC, beneficial owner, wire, contact, preference, commitment, and close documents data. Identify any investor type or jurisdiction-specific requirements, mark provider, due date, and reviewer for each item. Send a consolidated gap request list to the authorized party, the check on it. Checklist scope is reviewed against Enclient legal requirements.
Who reviews the checklist scope against Enclient legal requirements?

After that, we receive, log, and preserve documents. What we do: save each document in the controlled onboarding workspace. Log received date, version, document type, investor fund, and completeness status. Protect sensitive tax, beneficial owner, and banking data using approved access controls. Identify missing pages, signatures, dates, schedules, or inconsistent legal names. The check on it: every document is associated with the correct investor fund and latest version is identifiable.
What happens to a document item when you find missing pages or inconsistent information?

Then, we review subscription, commitment, side letter, and tax form completeness. What we do: confirm investor legal name, fund entity, commitment, close effective date, and signatures; compare side letter terms to the operational checklist and flag requirements affecting fees, notices, reporting, transfers, or allocations; confirm the submitted W-9/W-8 type, identity, signature date, and completeness; reconcile commitment and close date to client instruction; issue a consolidated deficiency list and track resolution. The check-on-it: no investor is marked document complete with missing signatures, material fields, or unresolved identity, commitment conflicts.
When you issue the consolidated deficiency list, how do you track each item through resolution?

Once that is done, we complete AML KYC clearance. What we do: submit the complete screening package to track missing ownership or risk records, resolve false positives or enhanced due diligence items through client channels, obtain written or system-recorded AML approval, rejection, or conditions, record clearance status and date in the onboarding checklist, the check-on-it, no capital accepted and no onboarding closed before AML clearance.
What happens to onboarding when AML clearance is rejected or comes with conditions?
